title: How to Clean and Maintain Refinished Hardwood Floors So They Last 20 Years
meta: Refinished hardwood can last 20 years: weekly vacuuming, pH-neutral cleaner, 35 to 55% humidity and a $1.99 recoat in time. Snohomish tips, Wills Flooring.
keywords: how to clean refinished hardwood floors, hardwood floor maintenance schedule, best cleaner for Bona finished floors, how often to recoat hardwood floors, hardwood floor care Snohomish WA

blocks.lead: Vacuum or dry-mop weekly, clean monthly with a pH-neutral hardwood cleaner and a barely damp microfiber pad, keep the house between 35 and 55 percent humidity, put felt under everything that moves, and book a screen and recoat every five to seven years before the finish wears through.
blocks.detail: Do those five things and a floor refinished with three coats of Bona water-based finish should never need another full sanding in your lifetime. Skip the recoat and you are back to $3.99 per sq ft instead of $1.99.

blocks.html: Snohomish is a hard place to own a hardwood floor. Gravel driveways, wet dogs, a wood stove that dries the house to the bone every January, and well water that leaves mineral spots on anything you mop with it. We have refinished floors from Fobes Hill to Clearview that looked ten years old after two, and others near Blackmans Lake that still look new at fifteen. The difference is never the wood. It is the routine. Here is the one we give every customer when we hand back the keys.

items.text: Stay off the floor. The last coat is dry to the touch in a few hours but soft underneath.
items.note: Socks only after 24 hours, no shoes, no pets.

items.text: Furniture can go back, lifted and set down, never dragged. Felt pads on every leg first.
Rugs and runners can go down. Use a natural rubber or felt pad underneath, never a rubber-backed bath mat.
The finish reaches full hardness. First damp cleaning happens now, not before.
items.note: Dry dust-mopping is fine any time after day 3.

blocks.note: Bona finished floors do not need polish, wax or restorer products. Those coat the finish and have to be stripped before the next recoat.

blocks.text: What should never touch the floor

items.title: Steam mops
items.text: Steam drives moisture into the seams and under the finish. It is the single fastest way to make a refinished floor go cloudy and cup at the edges. Every finish manufacturer excludes steam damage from the warranty.

items.title: Vinegar, ammonia and all-purpose cleaners
items.text: Vinegar is acidic and dulls water-based finish over time. Ammonia and general cleaners leave residue that shows as streaks in low light. Use a cleaner made for polyurethane floors and nothing else.

items.title: Oil soaps, polishes and restorers
items.text: They make a dull floor shine for a month, then build up, attract dirt and, worst of all, stop the next recoat from bonding. We have had to fully sand floors that only needed a $1.99 recoat because of a polish habit.

items.title: Wet mops and well water
items.text: A sopping mop leaves standing water in the board seams. Snohomish well water adds minerals that dry as white spots. Spray the pad, not the floor, and if your water is hard, use distilled water or a ready-mixed cleaner.

blocks.note: Choose Recoat for a floor with intact finish. If any spot is worn to bare wood, the natural rate applies to that room.

blocks.text: The 20-year plan: recoat before you sand

a.title: Do it now when
items: The finish looks dull or has fine surface scratches in traffic lanes
No spot is worn through to bare, gray or darkened wood
The floor has never been waxed, polished or oil-soaped
It has been five to seven years since the last coat
You want one day of work and no dust

b.title: You waited too long when
items: Bare wood shows in front of the sink, the door or the couch
Boards have gone gray or black from water sitting on raw wood
Deep scratches or dog nail gouges are into the wood, not the finish
A polish or wax product has been used and cannot be fully removed

blocks.text: Mistakes that shorten a refinish in a Snohomish house

items: Running the wood stove all winter with no humidifier. Indoor humidity drops into the twenties, boards shrink, and the gaps fill with grit that grinds the edges when the boards swell again in spring.
No walk-off mat inside the door from the gravel drive. Grit is the enemy, and one mat inside and one outside removes most of it before it reaches the floor.
Letting dog nails go. Trim them monthly; long nails cut finish, especially where the dog turns at the door.
Rolling office chairs with hard casters. Swap for soft urethane casters or use a mat.
Leaving a rug in the same south-facing spot for years. The floor around it darkens in the sun and the rug outline shows when you move it. Rotate rugs each season.
Waiting for the floor to look bad before calling. By the time the traffic lane is visibly worn, the recoat window has often closed.

blocks.title: Wood stove owners:
blocks.text: A kettle on the stove is not enough. Put a hygrometer in the room with the floor and add a humidifier when it reads under 35 percent. Engineered floors move about half as much as solid, but both gap in a dry house. If gaps have already opened, our post on fixing gaps during refinishing explains what can and cannot be filled.

items.html: Fall: Put out the mats, trim the dog's nails, set up the humidifier before the first fire, and replace felt pads.
Winter: Watch the hygrometer. Wipe up melted slush at the door the same day. Skip damp cleaning when the house is very dry; dust-mop instead.
Spring: First good damp clean of the year with pH-neutral cleaner. Move the rugs and check for sun lines.
Summer: Look at the traffic lanes in low-angle evening light. Dull but intact means it is time to book a recoat for fall.
Every 5 to 7 years: Screen and recoat at $1.99 per sq ft. Book it in the off-season and we can usually do a Snohomish main floor in one day. See our refinishing page for how it works.

faq.q: What is the best cleaner for refinished hardwood floors?
faq.a: A pH-neutral cleaner made for polyurethane hardwood floors, sprayed lightly on a microfiber pad. Bona makes one for its finishes and we recommend it, but any residue-free, water-based hardwood cleaner works. Avoid vinegar, ammonia, oil soaps, polishes and anything that promises shine.

faq.q: How often should refinished hardwood floors be recoated?
faq.a: Every five to seven years in a normal home, sooner with large dogs or heavy traffic. A screen and recoat at Wills Flooring is $1.99 per sq ft and only works while the old finish is intact, so the timing matters more than the calendar.

faq.q: Can I use a steam mop on refinished hardwood?
faq.a: No. Steam forces moisture into the seams and under the finish, causing cloudiness, cupping and finish failure. Finish manufacturers exclude steam damage from warranties. A barely damp microfiber pad with a hardwood cleaner does the same job safely.

faq.q: How long after refinishing can I mop the floor?
faq.a: Wait two weeks for the finish to fully harden before any damp cleaning, and 30 days to be safe. Dry dust-mopping is fine after the first few days. Socks after 24 hours, furniture after 72, rugs after a week.

faq.q: What humidity should I keep in the house for hardwood floors?
faq.a: Between 35 and 55 percent. Snohomish homes with wood stoves often drop below 30 in winter, which opens gaps. A whole-house or room humidifier keeps solid oak stable. Above 60 percent for long periods, boards can cup.

It fills and hides fine surface scratches that are in the finish only. Scratches that have cut into the wood, or that show as white lines, need a full sand to remove. The free estimate tells you which kind you have.
